implementation_notes: Scala has no ring buffer in the stdlib; mutable.Queue is a growable ring-backed deque (it wraps and resizes), ArrayDeque is a growable circular array, and for concurrency the choices are java.util.concurrent.ArrayBlockingQueue (bounded, blocking, lock-based) or a hand-written ring with AtomicLong/AtomicInteger and the acquire/release pattern. Scala's contribution is minimal: the type parameter makes the element type explicit, and for a numeric ring a primitive Array (Array[Double]) is the fixed, allocation-free backing store. For a real-time or audio ring, a hand-written Array-based ring with two AtomicInts is the construction, and Scala's immutable collections are not the right backing store (they allocate on every push, which defeats the ring). The choice: mutable.Queue for a single-threaded growable deque, ArrayBlockingQueue for a bounded blocking queue, hand-written Array ring for a measured hot path.
idiom_name: mutable.Queue / ArrayDeque (growable) or java.util.concurrent.ArrayBlockingQueue (bounded); hand-written Array ring with AtomicInt for a hot path
code_sketch:
import scala.collection.mutable
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong

// the stdlib growable deque (ring-backed, resizes):
val q = mutable.Queue[Int]()
q.enqueue(1); q.dequeue()

// bounded, blocking, multi-producer:
val bq = new java.util.concurrent.ArrayBlockingQueue[Int](256)

// hand-written SPSC ring for a measured hot path (fixed primitive array):
class SpscRing(val size: Int) {   // size a power of two
    require((size & (size - 1)) == 0, "power of two")
    private val buf = new Array[Double](size)   // fixed, primitive, no boxing
    private val mask = size - 1L
    private val head = new AtomicLong(0)          // producer-owned
    private val tail = new AtomicLong(0)          // consumer-owned
}
pitfalls: mutable.Queue and ArrayDeque are growable and allocate on growth - fine for a deque, wrong for a fixed-memory ring.
ArrayBlockingQueue takes a lock per operation - correct and simple, but it is the contention a ring avoids.
The two AtomicLong indices must be on separate cache lines for a real SPSC ring; Scala object layout does not guarantee it.
An immutable Scala collection as the ring's backing store allocates on every push, defeating the fixed-memory property entirely.
alternative: java.util.concurrent.ArrayBlockingQueue for a bounded, blocking, multi-producer ring; mutable.Queue for a single-threaded growable deque
